newsitem.title: GERMANY: Degussa posts strong 9-month profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Degussa posts strong 9-month profit rise.

text.p: German chemicals and metals group Degussa AG on Tuesday said full year 1996/97 results were likely to top last year's after nine-month profits jumped by a stronger than expected 30 percent.
In a statement Degussa reported nine month sales had climbed by 10 percent to 11.24 billion marks and pre-tax profits rose 30 percent to 374 million marks.

For the 1995/96 business year ending September 30, Degussa reported its second consecutive set of record pre-tax profits at 413 million marks. But sales had dipped by one percent to 13.79 billion marks.

Heading into the fourth quarter of the current business year, Degussa said the favourable earnings situation should continue and full year results should "again exceed the already good earnings of the previous year".
Degussa shares, up more than 20 percent since mid-June, opened Frankfurt bourse trading at a record 106 marks. But profit-taking soon set in, taking the price back to 103.50 marks.
At the same time the broader DAX index was trading down 0.18 percent at 4,392.49 points.

Traders and analysts agreed Tuesday's better than expected nine-month results had lubricated the share's rise, but noted the engine for gains remained speculation over how Degussa's largest shareholder Veba AG might help revamp the company.

Breaking down its results, Degussa said sales in the health and nutrition segment climbed 13 percent to 2.3 billion marks while "earnings grew significantly". Higher demand for feed additives and products from Degussa's dental division were largely responsible for the increase, the group said.
On the other hand Degussa's Asta Medica Group again suffered from sluggish domestic demand which pulled earnings below year ago levels.
Analysts expect Degussa will soon try to either sell or merge the Asta unit as it stands little chance of achieving quickly the critical mass a drugs group needs to survive.

"Degussa cannot wait much longer to do something with this unit, Asta has a limited pipeline and is turning into a drag, something Veba will likely not tolerate for long," said an analyst who asked not to be named.

Degussa's chemicals business, posting an 11 percent rise in nine-month sales to 3.2 billion marks and stronger earnings, benefited from higher volume sales and improved exchange rates. A weaker mark makes German products less expensive abroad, and this is likely to make a relatively big impact on 1997 company profits.

Prices in the chemicals sector however remained marginally lower, the group added. "We were able to expand our chemicals business notably in all regions, especially with strong volume gains in North America," Degussa said.
In its precious metals and banking sector, sales, excluding precious metals trading and adjusted for compositional changes of consolidated companies, matched last year's levels.

"Earnings improved due to the absence of restructuring costs in this fiscal year and a noticeable upturn of the operational results in the precious metals and auto catalysts divisions and the Cerdec group," Degussa said.

Analysts speculated that the acquisition of a 36.4 percent stake in Degussa by Veba, the diversified German utility, may prompt consideration of major changes in the chemicals division and precious metals sector.
Degussa announced last week it may separate its precious metals group into a separate legal entity, as part of plans to raise the group's earnings potential and attractiveness for investors.
